measurement.merge_identity: unit, algorithm-shell, and graph-top points are merged only for the same layout and declaration; integration evidence additionally requires a current top-level DUT hash and a coverage artifact newer than the declaration
measurement.point_key: declaration path, coverage page, line, column, objective, and source range; hierarchy is intentionally removed when merging identical declarations
measurement.denominator_rule: every context/module/source-hash raw point count is pinned; missing, changed, or stale labels fail closure
measurement.census_rule: each zero point must match exactly one structural rule; unmatched or multiply matched points fail closure, and every rule must match at least one concrete zero

rules.reason: The unsigned remaining-vertex count is either greater than CACHELINE_VERTEX_NUM or less than/equal to it; the implicit final else arm of the else-if chain is structurally impossible.

The pinned unit topology launches at most CU_VERTEX_JOB_BUFFER_SIZE vertices and cacheline-sized shifts, so upper offset, sequence, shift-limit, and boundary bits outside that exact bound cannot toggle.
The exact filter scenario count is bounded by the filter FIFO depth, so upper filtered-counter bits are outside the fixed unit topology.
Each producer stops at almost-full and each command phase has fewer entries than its staging depth, so the corresponding full flags and unreachable staging almost-full flags cannot assert.

Residual else arms are either the impossible final arm of an unsigned greater-than/less-than-or-equal partition or require a duplicate response while a prior cacheline is still shifting, which the command/response ownership protocol forbids.

The active edge unit topology bounds a launch to CU_EDGE_JOB_BUFFER_SIZE entries and a cacheline-sized shift; upper address, sequence, remainder, and shift-control bits outside that bound are padding for these fixed contexts.
Almost-full backpressure and the one-cacheline response phase prevent these staging FIFOs from reaching the remaining almost-full/full states.

For a two-slot tagged pair buffer, an emitting slot is necessarily non-empty, same-tag simultaneous halves bypass the second allocator, and different tags cannot both own the slot selected by the first half. The residual short-circuit combinations are therefore impossible.
Source, destination, and high-component requests are selected by mutually exclusive pending-count and comp_low_ready states; residual short-circuit combinations contradict those state invariants.
The fixed component scenario bounds job identifiers and the equal-component continuation count; remaining upper counter and identifier bits are outside the pinned topology.
EdgeComponentRead is used only as an internal payload aggregate; its valid member is never the ownership signal and is intentionally left constant.

The first component-update stages carry only comp_high or the computed comp_low; comp_comp_high is introduced after the high-component read, and the earlier placeholder members are intentionally constant.

The producer observes almost-full and the component engine permits at most two ordinary reads plus one high-component read in flight, below the command and edge staging depths; remaining full/almost-full flags cannot assert.

Command tags and unused metadata are zero, command type/array/size fields are fixed enums or constants, and address/auxiliary upper bits are padding above the property index/data widths. Exercised variable bits are retained in the reachable denominator.
offset_data is eight bits wide but only the cacheline-half selector width is reachable for every active property element size; remaining bits are padding.
The BFS write pipeline removes upstream grant as soon as any staging FIFO is almost-full, so the remaining input almost-full/full and downstream full flags cannot assert.

Verilator records these unpacked-array input bits but does not attribute the testbench whole-array assignments to every element bit; the corresponding latched/reduced production signals provide the behavioral evidence.
The backend emits zero toggle records for unpacked routed output/status elements even when direct one-hot ownership assertions and coordinate sweeps exercise each element.
The shared EdgeDataRead/EdgeDataWrite tagged unions expose data, data_1, data_2, weight, source, destination, and index aliases, but each active algorithm drives only its selected payload members.
CU coordinates on scheduler-generated payloads are fixed by CU_ID parameters or the selected topology owner; bits outside the active coordinate encoding are constant.
The exact active topology contains four or five CUs and the directed counter values are bounded; upper per-CU and reduced counter bits outside that sum range are width padding for these contexts.

The residual ready/request bits are aliases for coordinates absent from a given four/five-CU elaboration or registered request mirrors whose asserted owner is proven by the direct one-hot and fairness scoreboards.

Ownership of the shared read and write command buses is only taken while the buffer that owner feeds is below its almost-full threshold, and the fifo keeps its headroom above that threshold, so the full flag of those command buffers and of every broadcast copy of their status cannot assert.
